newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, U.S. to hold talks on medical equipment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, U.S. to hold talks on medical equipment.

text.p: Taiwan and the United States will hold talks on the imports of American medical equipment after U.S. firms accused Taipei of blocking the entry of such imports, a trade official said on Wednesday.

David Burns, a senior adviser to the U.S. trade representative, is scheduled to meet with Taiwan's Board of Foreign Trade on Friday and visit the island's Health Insurance Bureau on Saturday, board official Chu Hsi said.

"We will explain Taiwan's health care system to the U.S. side at the meeting," Chu said by telephone, adding that there was some "misunderstanding" between the two sides over imports of U.S. medical equipment.
U.S. medical equipment makers have accused Taiwan's Health Insurance Bureau of unfairly dominating the market, and the United States has started looking into the complaints, he said.
Chu denied the accusations, saying the bureau had not put any restrictions on imports of U.S. medical equipments.

If Washington decides Taiwan's national health care system is a monopoly impeding U.S. products, it would review the case before announcing at the end of September the "301 list" of countries it sees as conducting unfair trade, Chu said.
Washington has removed Taiwan from the "watch list" under the Special 301 provision of U.S. trade law, under which it can impose sanctions.
But Taiwan remains in a lower category on the general 301 list, which lets Washington respond to what it sees as the inadequate protection of intellectual property rights.
